Definition: probably strengthened from ψάω (to rub or touch the surface; compare G5597); to twitch or twang, i.e. to play on a stringed instrument (celebrate the divine worship with music and accompanying odes):--make melody, sing (psalms).
BiblicalUsage: Psallo means to twang, to play on a stringed instrument, and so to sing praise with melody. Paul says to speak to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord, and, I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the understanding also; James says the merry man should sing psalms. And the Gentiles are to glorify God for His mercy, as it is written, For this cause I will confess to Thee among the Gentiles, and sing unto Thy name.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe singing is the sound of the word dwelling in me: when Christ's word is rich in my heart, it comes out as melody. I hold that the merry Christian sings because he cannot help it, and the Gentile sings because mercy has reached him too.
